ruleAssertGrammar.why: DESIGN.md §8 shows `assert` as a string, and a rules component plus generated tests has to be derivable from it. So `assert` is a string in ONE closed grammar — not prose. A ~60-line recursive-descent parser in the template compiles every assert below; an assert that does not parse is a build failure, not a review comment.
terms: <field>                              scalar field of the control record (or of the item, inside forall/exists)
record.<field>                       explicit control-record scope from inside forall/exists
minorUnitScale(<currencyField>)      10^exponent from the ONE ISO 4217 table of DESIGN.md §6
ruleAssertGrammar.arithmetic: + - * ONLY. There is no division operator in this grammar, by design: division is where silent rounding enters a money path. Every ratio comparison below is written as a cross-multiplication instead. The generator emits Math.addExact/Math.multiplyExact so an overflow throws rather than wraps.
ruleAssertGrammar.predicates: == != < <= > >= | and or not implies | present(<field>) absent(<field>) | <field> in (<lit>, ...) | forall(<arrayField>, <itemExpr>) | exists(<arrayField>, <itemExpr>)
ruleAssertGrammar.precedence: not > comparison > and > or > implies; parentheses allowed
ruleAssertGrammar.dateVsTimestamp: Comparing a `date` against a `timestamp` compares the timestamp's date in the record's stated timezone (UTC). The generator must emit that coercion once, in the evaluator.
ruleAssertGrammar.tests: Each rule carries examples.pass and examples.fail — partial records over the rule's own fields. The template generates one passing and one failing test per rule from them. A rule with no examples is a rule with no test, so examples are mandatory.
ruleAssertGrammar.onViolation: EXACTLY the two values DESIGN.md §8 locks: `reject` (refuse the write, 422) and `flag` (accept, raise a finding, append an immutable audit row, and queue a referral). `flag` is this estate's realisation of the research's REFER outcome — no third enum value was invented.

conventions.rejectVersusFlag: A deliberate split, and the most important editorial decision in this fragment. `reject` is used ONLY for (a) arithmetic and ledger identities, (b) internal contradictions in the record's own claims, (c) missing evidence/attribution that a cited standard requires, and (d) the Islamic landscape's own stated constraint that there are no interest-bearing constructs. `flag` is used for EVERY contested or jurisdictionally divergent Shariah position. Rationale: a `reject` on a contested ruling is the code issuing a fatwa. The code applies SSB-approved criteria and records which criteria and which version; it does not decide.
conventions.sharedItemShapesScope: The keys of sharedItemShapes are FRAGMENT-SCOPED and prefixed `Treasury` so they cannot collide with the other four business-area fragments. Whether the merged catalog unifies these shapes across areas is the catalog owner's merge-time call, not this agent's.
conventions.shariahReviewStatus: Every `shariah` block below is reviewed:false. Per DESIGN.md §7: a profit-sharing, capital-at-risk or screening field modelled by a developer is a compliance claim the code cannot back. Nothing here is signed off by any Shariah supervisory board.
conventions.citationDiscipline: Each rule carries `citation` and `citationStatus`. citationStatus is one of: `research-supported` (the clause or a verbatim quote of it is in the WAVE 3 / shariah research on disk), `title-only` (the standard's number and title are research-confirmed but the clause text was not obtained), `unverified` (named in ISLAMIC-MASTER-CATALOG.md or classically held, with NO primary text obtained in this research), or `estate-constraint` (not a Shariah ruling at all — an invariant this project itself declares). serviceDomains.name: Sukuk Issuance
serviceDomains.summary: Structures and issues a sukuk program. The whole design turns on one distinction the master catalog's own use cases demand and a bond model cannot carry: AssetBacked (true sale, holders own the asset) versus AssetBased (beneficial interest only, recourse to the obligor). Everything else — the structure enum, the underlying-asset pool with per-asset ownership transfer, the no-principal-guarantee invariant, the face-value purchase-undertaking flag — exists to make that distinction evidenced rather than asserted.

fields.name: originatorPartyRef
fields.note: the asset originator, which is routinely NOT the issuing SPV — keeping them as separate fields is what makes the true-sale question askable

fields.name: assetBackingBasis
fields.note: The single most load-bearing field in this business area. AssetBacked = legal true sale, certificate holders have recourse to the asset. AssetBased = beneficial ownership only, recourse to the obligor. AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard 62 (Sukuk) — an EXPOSURE DRAFT as of Nov 2026, research-confirmed — is understood to push toward real ownership transfer, so this field is deliberately explicit rather than inferred, to absorb a later requirement without a migration of meaning.

fields.name: trueSaleEvidenceRef
fields.note: legal-opinion / transfer-deed reference; required when assetBackingBasis = AssetBacked

fields.name: debtBasedUnderlying
fields.note: true when sukukStructure is MurabahaSukuk | SalamSukuk | IstisnaSukuk — i.e. the certificate represents a receivable. Carried as data because the secondary-trading question differs for debt-based certificates.

fields.name: certificateCurrency
fields.note: ISO 4217 alpha-3; governs every money field on this record

fields.name: expectedPeriodicDistributionBps
fields.note: EXACT basis points, never a float. This is an expectation, not a contractual rate — see distributionIsIndicative and rule ISB-SUK-ISS-07.

fields.name: mudaribProfitShareRatio
fields.note: The manager's/mudarib's share of PROFIT as an exact numerator/denominator. The certificate holders' share is the complement (denominator - numerator)/denominator, so the two shares sum to 1 by construction rather than by a validation that can be skipped. It is a share of profit and never a percentage of the certificate's face value — the research cites SS 13 §8/1 for that distinction.

fields.note: the contractual CEILING on the manager's share. IFSB GN-3 fn.12/13 per the research: the contractual PSR is a ceiling, the realised share may be lower, and a unilateral increase above it is not permitted.

uncertain: AGGREGATE CONCENTRATION CANNOT BE EXPRESSED. A per-record rule grammar has no group-by, so 'no single issuer above N bps' is not assertable as a rule over this control record. Rather than inventing a groupSum operator for one case, concentration is computed by a read projection and RECORDED in limitBreaches, and the rules guard that ledger (ISB-SUK-PRT-02/03). If aggregate limits must be enforced at write time, the catalog needs a first-class `aggregates` block and the template a query generator — that is a schema decision for the catalog owner, not something to smuggle in as a free-text assert.

MANDATE CONFORMANCE IS NOT ASSERTED AND NO PLACEHOLDER RULE PRETENDS IT IS. 'Every position's structure must be in permittedStructures' is a join between two sibling arrays, which the grammar cannot express. A rule for it was drafted and then REMOVED, because an assert that does not parse under this fragment's own grammar is a build failure rather than a visible gap, and a rule that silently checks something weaker is worse than an honest absence. The check belongs in the mandate projection alongside concentration.

PER and IRR are NOT modelled here even though a Mudarabah-managed portfolio feeding an investment pool is exactly where smoothing is applied. They belong to isb-profit-equalization-reserve and isb-investment-risk-reserve in the Deposits area. The ordering is normative (PER before the mudarib share and shared with shareholders; IRR after the mudarib share, in IAH equity, usable only for IAH investment losses — GN-3 ¶20/25-27, IFSB-30 ¶256) and getting the sequence wrong changes every number downstream, so it must be owned in ONE place. Cross-area coordination needed.
BNM ¶13.5 forbids smoothing/DCR outright. Any PER/IRR interaction with this portfolio must be feature-flagged off per jurisdiction, which is a platform concern this entry does not express.

minAverageRatingNotch assumes an institution-internal integer scale. Mapping agency ratings onto it is configuration this entry does not model, and whether a conventional credit rating is an appropriate input at all was not researched.

Performance attribution, duration/profit-rate sensitivity and stress testing are absent. Modelling profit-rate duration for sukuk raises a prior question (whether a conventional rate-sensitivity measure is the right frame) that was not researched.

serviceDomains.name: Interbank Commodity Murabaha Desk
serviceDomains.summary: Interbank liquidity placed and taken through commodity Murabaha (Tawarruq) instead of an interest-bearing deposit. The design is built around the one clause this research actually supports for the structure: Murabaha sequencing must show possession and risk transfer BEFORE the onward sale. So the legs are a first-class, ordered sub-resource with per-leg titleTransferred and riskBorneByBank, and the sequencing rule compares the ordinal of the spot purchase against the ordinal of the onward sale. The deferred sale price is a fixed total with cost and profit disclosed separately and an explicit accruesOnArrears = false invariant.

fields.name: direction
fields.note: Placement: the bank places liquidity — it buys the commodity spot and sells it onward on deferred payment, so the counterparty owes the deferred price. Taking: the mirror. The direction decides which leg the bank holds and therefore which party's possession must be evidenced.

fields.name: masterAgreementType
fields.note: IIFM master agreements are named in ISLAMIC-MASTER-CATALOG.md's integration list; NO primary IIFM document was obtained in this research, so the enum records which framework was used and claims nothing about its content.

fields.name: commodityIsGoldOrSilver
fields.note: carried explicitly because gold and silver are classically treated as currency-like (ribawi), which would make a deferred-payment sale of them a currency-exchange problem rather than a commodity sale. No primary clause was obtained — see rule ISB-IMD-09.

fields.name: costPriceMinor
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 8 §4/3 per the research: the cost price and the profit are disclosed, not just a total

fields.name: deferredSalePriceMinor
fields.note: a FIXED total sale price, never an accruing balance — see accruesOnArrears and ISB-IMD-03

fields.name: profitEquivalentBps
fields.note: the 'profit rate equivalent' a desk quotes to compare deals. EXACT bps. It is a disclosure artefact and never a contractual accrual rate — see ISB-IMD-10.

fields.name: possessionTakenBasis
fields.note: 'None' is the structural failure the rules exist to catch

fields.name: possessionEvidenceRef
fields.note: warrant / e-certificate / platform reference

fields.name: accruesOnArrears
fields.note: must be false. The research states the invariant plainly: outstandingAmount is a fixed total sale price, never an accruing balance, and 'accruesOnArrears: false' is an explicit, testable invariant (SS 47 §5).

fields.name: latePaymentCharityUndertakingMinor
fields.note: a NON-INCOME line. The research cites SS 3 §2/1/8 for the charity undertaking and notes stricter opinions reject it entirely — so the rules assert its ROUTING, never its permissibility.

fields.name: recoveryCostsDueMinor
fields.note: a NON-INCOME line, separate from the charity undertaking (SS 3 §2/1/4 per the research)

items.name: sequenceNo
items.note: the ordinal the sequencing rule compares — an explicit integer, not an inference from a timestamp that may be equal to the microsecond

items.name: riskBorneByBank
items.note: the field that makes 'the bank actually owned the commodity' checkable rather than assumed

rules.statement: The deferred sale price must equal cost plus profit, both disclosed.
rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 8 §4/3 (via the research's data-model recommendation): the outstanding amount is a fixed total sale price with profitAmount and costPrice disclosed. Clause text not independently obtained.

rules.statement: Profit on a Murabaha cannot be negative.
rules.citation: none — invariant

rules.statement: The deferred price does not accrue on arrears.
rules.citation: Research, verbatim: "Add `accruesOnArrears: false` as an explicit, testable invariant (SS 47 §5)."

rules.statement: Possession must precede the onward sale.
rules.assert: present(possessionTimestamp) and present(onwardSaleTimestamp) and possessionTimestamp < onwardSaleTimestamp
rules.citation: Research, verbatim: "Murabaha sequencing must show possession/risk transfer before onward sale (SS 8 §3/2)."

rules.statement: Possession must have been taken on some basis.
rules.citation: SS 8 §3/2 as above (research-supported).

rules.statement: The bank must have actually owned and borne the risk on the commodity.
rules.assert: exists(legs, legType == 'SpotPurchase' and titleTransferred == true and riskBorneByBank == true)
rules.citation: SS 8 §3/2 as above (research-supported) — possession AND risk transfer.

rules.statement: The spot purchase leg must be sequenced before the onward sale leg.
rules.assert: min(legs.sequenceNo where legType == 'SpotPurchase') < min(legs.sequenceNo where legType == 'OnwardSale')
rules.citation: SS 8 §3/2 as above (research-supported). This is the leg-level realisation of ISB-IMD-04: a timestamp pair can be equal to the microsecond on an automated platform, so an explicit ordinal is also asserted.

rules.statement: A binding bilateral promise needs Shariah review.
rules.citation: Research names this as a live divergence: 'binding bilateral promise in Murabaha forbidden (SS 8 §2/3/1) vs permitted in Pakistan by the SBP amendment note', and instructs that all such divergences be 'configuration with a named authority, not defaults'.
rules.rationale: flag, never reject: the research explicitly lists this as a position the code must not resolve.

rules.statement: A deferred-payment sale of gold or silver needs Shariah review.
rules.citation: The classical treatment of gold and silver as currency-like (ribawi) commodities, which would make a deferred sale of them a currency-exchange question. NO primary text was obtained in this research.
rules.rationale: flag despite being widely held, for exactly the reason the hard rules give: a reject on an unverified ruling is the code issuing a fatwa.

rules.statement: A quoted profit-rate equivalent must be marked disclosure-only.
rules.citation: Research: the component 'must not ... present an expected/indicative rate as a declared rate (SS 47 §7/2, SS 45 §3/6, BNM ¶24.5)'.

rules.statement: Settled plus outstanding must equal the deferred sale price.
rules.citation: none — ledger identity. This is the identity that makes ISB-IMD-03 meaningful: with no accrual, the total never moves.

rules.statement: Scheduled settlement instructions cannot exceed the deferred sale price.
rules.citation: none — ledger identity

rules.statement: Quarantined non-compliance income must be routed to a charity pool and never funded from investment-account-holder funds.
rules.assert: forall(shariahFindings, (status == 'IncomeQuarantined' implies (present(quarantinedAmountMinor) and present(charityPoolRef))) and fundedFromIahPool == false)
rules.citation: Research: 'SNC income and late-payment charity must sit in a segregated liability, never in P&L, and never be funded from IAH pool funds (SS 13 §9/6).'

rules.statement: A late-payment charity undertaking must name the charity pool it is routed to.
rules.citation: Research cites SS 3 §2/1/8 for the charity undertaking and §2/1/4 for recovery costs, both as separate NON-INCOME lines, and states that late-payment charity must never sit in P&L.
rules.rationale: The rule asserts ROUTING, not permissibility: the research also records that stricter opinions reject the charity undertaking entirely, so whether it may be taken at all is an SSB determination, not this rule's business.

rules.statement: Tenor and maturity must be consistent and positive.
rules.citation: none — internal consistency

rules.statement: Legs in a currency other than the trade currency need an explicit conversion decision.
rules.citation: DESIGN.md §6. The 3-decimal Gulf currencies (BHD, KWD, OMR, TND) are the first test case precisely because they break a hardcoded x100.

rules.statement: Each leg's consideration must equal quantity times unit price.
rules.citation: none — arithmetic identity, flagged rather than rejected because platform conventions quote a unit price per lot with its own rounding, so exactness depends on a rounding policy that belongs in the money module (DESIGN.md §6), not here.

shariah.contractTypeGap: The structure is TAWARRUQ (commodity Murabaha with an onward monetising sale). DESIGN.md §7 locks the ContractType enum to ten values and 'Tawarruq' is not among them, while the research's own recommended enum DOES include TAWARRUQ. DESIGN.md wins, so contractType is 'Murabaha' — the underlying contract — and the Tawarruq character is carried as DATA (commodityPlatform, the leg sequence, promiseType) rather than as an invented enum value. REPORTED GAP: §7's enum and the research's enum disagree, and §7's should probably gain Tawarruq.
shariah.capitalAtRiskMeaning: Once the onward sale completes, the counterparty owes a FIXED, certain deferred price — a receivable, not a profit-sharing exposure, so the amount is not capital at risk in the DESIGN.md §7 sense. Two honest qualifications: (a) during the commodity-ownership window the desk genuinely does bear asset risk, which is the whole point of SS 8 §3/2 and of riskBorneByBank; (b) counterparty CREDIT risk is real and is not what capitalAtRisk means here.

uncertain: TAWARRUQ ITSELF IS CONTESTED AND THIS ENTRY DOES NOT ADJUDICATE IT. Organised Tawarruq is the subject of well-known adverse resolutions by some fiqh bodies while remaining standard interbank practice in several markets. This research retrieved NO Tawarruq-specific standard, so there is no rule here that passes judgement on the structure. What the rules do instead is make the structure's integrity checkable: did the bank take possession, did it bear risk, did the legs happen in the right order, is the price fixed. If an SSB rules the structure impermissible, that is a policy decision above this service domain, not a rule inside it.

The deferred sale price's presence in the enum does not establish that a Tawarruq commodity sale is a genuine sale rather than a form. The commodityPlatform field records which market facility was used; it is not evidence of a real commodity market.

The ribawi (gold/silver) rule in ISB-IMD-09 has no primary citation and is therefore a flag. If the owner obtains the clause, it can be promoted to a reject by changing one field in this entry — which is the point of keeping rules as data.

Early settlement rebate (ibra') is NOT modelled. A rebate on early settlement of a fixed deferred price is common and its permissibility and whether it may be contractually promised are both contested. Adding an ibra' field without a named authority would be inventing a compliance claim.

Direction (Placement/Taking) changes which party's possession must be evidenced, but the rules as written check the bank's possession on the SpotPurchase leg regardless. For a Taking the counterparty is the one taking possession first, so ISB-IMD-06 is too strong in that direction. This is a real modelling gap: it should become two rules gated on `direction`, and is left flagged here rather than silently fixed with an unverified assumption about who evidences what.

Netting of offsetting interbank Murabaha deals is not modelled. Set-off against a customer account 'requires the same currency or the prevailing rate (SS 3 §2/5/3)' per the research, which suggests netting needs its own rules; none are asserted.

serviceDomains.name: Islamic FX Wad Arrangements
serviceDomains.summary: FX exposure managed with a unilateral promise (Wa'd) rather than a forward contract. Two design decisions carry the weight. First, the FX rate is an EXACT integer numerator/denominator, never a float — and the rate-consistency check uses minorUnitScale() on BOTH currencies, because a cross-currency minor-unit comparison with a hardcoded x100 is wrong for every 3-decimal Gulf currency. Second, the record's own claims are made mutually checkable: an arrangement that calls itself unilateral cannot also bind both parties. That is an internal contradiction and is rejected; every contested Shariah position is flagged.

fields.name: promisorParty
fields.note: a unilateral promise has exactly ONE promisor; recording who gave it is what makes 'unilateral' falsifiable

fields.name: masterAgreementType
fields.note: IIFM/ISDA Tahawwut is named in ISLAMIC-MASTER-CATALOG.md's integration list; NO primary document was obtained in this research, so this records which framework was used and claims nothing about its content.

fields.name: promisedRate
fields.note: an EXACT integer numerator/denominator. An FX rate as a float or a decimal string is the single most common way a money path loses precision, and a rate legitimately exceeds 1, which is why `rate` exists separately from `ratio`.

fields.name: rateQuoteConvention
fields.note: without this the rate is ambiguous and the consistency check is unwritable

fields.name: netSettlementPermitted
fields.note: if net cash settlement is permitted there may be no actual currency exchange at all, which makes the arrangement a cash-settled payoff rather than a sale — see ISB-WAD-05

items.name: bothLegsDelivered
items.note: the honest field: a currency exchange in which both legs were not actually delivered is not an exchange

rules.statement: An arrangement that calls itself unilateral cannot bind both parties.
rules.citation: none — internal contradiction in the record's own claims, NOT a Shariah ruling
rules.rationale: This is the clearest example of the reject/flag split in this fragment. A promise binding both parties is a bilateral promise; a record asserting both is incoherent regardless of anyone's fiqh position, so rejecting it issues no ruling. Whether a binding bilateral promise is permissible is ISB-WAD-02, and that one flags.

rules.statement: A binding bilateral promise needs Shariah review.
rules.citation: The research names the binding-bilateral-promise divergence for MURABAHA (SS 8 §2/3/1 forbids; SBP amendment note permits in Pakistan) and instructs that such divergences be configuration with a named authority. The FX/currency analogue was NOT obtained in this research, so the citation is by analogy only.

rules.statement: An FX arrangement needs two different currencies.
rules.citation: none — internal consistency

rules.statement: The promised amounts must be consistent with the promised rate, across both currencies' minor-unit exponents.
rules.assert: rateQuoteConvention == 'BuyPerSell' implies sellAmountMinor * promisedRate.numerator * minorUnitScale(buyCurrency) == buyAmountMinor * promisedRate.denominator * minorUnitScale(sellCurrency)
rules.citation: DESIGN.md §6 — one conversion function, the ISO 4217 exponent from an explicit table, property-based round-trip tests, and the 3-decimal Gulf currencies as the first test case.
rules.rationale: The reason this is the most important rule in this entry: BHD/KWD/OMR/TND are 3-decimal and JPY is 0-decimal, so comparing minor units across a currency pair WITHOUT both exponents is wrong, silently, and in a money path. It is a `flag` rather than a `reject` for one honest reason: exactness here depends on a documented rounding policy, and that policy belongs in the single money-conversion module of DESIGN.md §6, not in a catalog entry. Promote to reject once that policy and its tolerance exist.

rules.statement: Net cash settlement without an actual currency exchange needs Shariah review.
rules.citation: A currency exchange with no delivery of either currency is a cash-settled payoff rather than a sale. NO primary clause on bay' al-sarf settlement was obtained in this research.

rules.statement: A forward value date on a currency exchange needs Shariah review.
rules.citation: The spot-settlement requirement for a currency exchange (bay' al-sarf) is the reason the Wa'd structure exists at all. NO primary text was obtained in this research, so this is a flag with a named concern, not an enforced ruling.

rules.statement: A speculative purpose needs Shariah review.
rules.citation: none — no clause obtained. Recorded as an explicit enum value rather than left implicit, because 'hedging' and 'positioning' are the same mechanics with different intent and only the record can state which.

rules.statement: A hedge must name the exposure it hedges.
rules.citation: none — evidence-for-a-claim invariant

rules.statement: A hedge larger than its exposure is a position, not a hedge.
rules.assert: present(hedgedExposureAmountMinor) and hedgedExposureCurrency == sellCurrency implies sellAmountMinor <= hedgedExposureAmountMinor
rules.citation: none — flagged, and deliberately gated on a matching currency because comparing amounts across currencies needs the one conversion function (DESIGN.md §6), which a rule must not inline

rules.statement: An exercised arrangement must have at least one recorded exchange execution.
rules.citation: none — ledger integrity. A promise recorded as exercised with no exchange is the exact shape of a cash-settled derivative dressed as a sale.

rules.statement: The exercise window must be ordered and not start before the promise.
rules.citation: none — internal consistency

rules.statement: A single unilateral promise has at most one leg.
rules.citation: none — internal consistency

rules.statement: An agreed compensation formula on breach needs Shariah review.
rules.citation: An agreed formula rather than actual loss resembles a derivative payoff. The actual-loss-only position is the AAOIFI-leaning one; NO clause was obtained in this research.

rules.statement: Both legs of an exchange should actually be delivered.
rules.citation: Same concern as ISB-WAD-05, asserted on the execution record rather than the permission. No primary clause obtained.

rules.statement: A unilateral promise has exactly one promisor and it must be recorded.
rules.citation: none — evidence-for-a-claim invariant

shariah.contractTypeGap: NO VALUE IN DESIGN.md §7's TEN-VALUE ENUM FITS, AND THIS IS REPORTED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. A Wa'd is a PROMISE, not one of the ten named contracts, and the exchange it promises is a currency sale (bay' al-sarf), which is also absent from the enum. Labelling this 'Murabaha' or 'Wakala' to fill the field would be a false statement in a compliance field, so contractType is null and the gap is named. RECOMMENDATION to the owner of §7: the enum needs either `Sarf`, or a separate `promiseType` dimension beside contractType. Mechanically, null is fine — a nullable TEXT column with a CHECK over the ten values plus NULL.
shariah.capitalAtRiskMeaning: A promise creates no capital exposure until it is exercised, and the executed exchange is a sale of one currency for another, not a profit-sharing investment. Market risk between promise and exercise is real and is not what capitalAtRisk means in DESIGN.md §7.

uncertain: THIS IS THE WEAKEST-GROUNDED ENTRY IN THE AREA AND SHOULD BE READ THAT WAY. Not one AAOIFI or IFSB clause on currency exchange or on promises was obtained by this research. Every Shariah-bearing rule here is a `flag` with the citation marked unverified; the only `reject`s are internal-contradiction and ledger checks. If the owner wants enforceable FX rules, the prerequisite is the primary text of the currency-trading and promise standards, not more modelling.

The SellPerBuy mirror is a second rule that is deliberately NOT written here, because writing it without a stated rounding policy would double the surface of an assert that is already a flag. One rule, honestly scoped, beats two that both need a policy that does not exist yet.

Rounding tolerance for ISB-WAD-04 is unresolved and is the reason it flags rather than rejects. The tolerance belongs in the single money-conversion module of DESIGN.md §6 with its property-based tests, not as a field in this catalog.

A Wa'd series (UnilateralWadSeries) covering a schedule of future exchanges is modelled as repeated legs. Whether a series of unilateral promises is materially different from a forward strip is exactly the question a scholar would ask and this entry cannot answer it.

No modelling of collateral, margin or credit support. Margin on an Islamic hedging arrangement raises its own questions (whether margin is a permissible security, how it is held) and none were researched.

serviceDomains.name: Shariah Compliant Liquidity Management
serviceDomains.summary: The bank's liquidity buffer and maturity ladder built only from Shariah-compliant instruments. The one rule here that is a hard reject on Shariah-adjacent grounds is also the one that needs no fatwa: this landscape's own catalog note says it contains no interest-bearing constructs, so an interest-bearing placement value above zero is a violation of the estate's own stated constraint. Everything contested — a legacy conventional instrument in the buffer, whether a given central-bank facility qualifies, an LCR breach — is flagged and referred.

fields.name: lcrBps
fields.note: EXACT basis points. A coverage ratio as a float is the same class of bug as a money float.

fields.name: lcrFloorBps
fields.note: the regulatory floor as CONFIGURATION, not a constant in code — it differs by jurisdiction

fields.name: interestBearingPlacementValueMinor
fields.note: must be zero — see ISB-LQM-01

items.name: contractType

rules.statement: An Islamic liquidity plan holds no interest-bearing placements.
rules.citation: The Islamic landscape's OWN stated constraint, from catalog/islamic-service-landscape.json `note`: 'no interest-bearing constructs — profit-sharing (Mudarabah/Musharakah), cost-plus sale (Murabaha), leasing (Ijara), and fee-based (Ujrah/Wakala) structures instead.'
rules.rationale: A reject that needs no fatwa: it enforces a constraint this project declares about itself, not a scholarly ruling it has no authority to issue.

rules.statement: A conventional instrument in the buffer needs Shariah review.
rules.citation: Same estate constraint as ISB-LQM-01, but a transition-period or inherited buffer can legitimately hold a legacy instrument pending wind-down, and the wind-down is an SSB determination (IFSB-31 Principle 10, rectification).

rules.statement: The buffer total should reconcile to the sum of positions.
rules.citation: none — flagged rather than rejected because the accounting scope of a 'liquid buffer' and the sum of recorded positions legitimately differ (accrued items, in-flight settlement), and the reconciliation tolerance is an accounting-policy parameter

rules.statement: An encumbered asset is not liquid.
rules.citation: none — structural, not Shariah: an asset pledged elsewhere cannot simultaneously be counted as available liquidity

rules.statement: Every position must be funded from the plan's own investment pool.
rules.citation: AAOIFI FAS 47 'Transfer of Assets between Investment Pools' — research-confirmed by number and title as governing pool-boundary integrity; clause text NOT obtained.
rules.rationale: Rejected for the same reason as ISB-SUK-PRT-04: the alternative is silent cross-pool subsidy between distinct sets of investment-account holders, which is a data-integrity failure as well as a Shariah one. An inter-pool transfer should be an explicit recorded transfer, not a field mismatch nobody notices.

rules.statement: A Qard Hassan placement is repayable at par and bears no capital risk.
rules.citation: Research's data-model recommendation: `capitalGuaranteed` is 'true only for Qard/Wadiah'.

rules.statement: A Mudarabah interbank placement bears capital risk.
rules.citation: Research: lossBearer ACCOUNT_HOLDER is 'mandatory for Mudarabah/Musharakah per SS 13 §8/7 and SS 45 §3/4'. IFSB GN-3 fn.12 (citing IFSB-2 ¶76) adds that the IIFS as Mudarib 'is not permitted to absorb losses incurred on the IAH's investment ... except in the case of misconduct or negligence'.
rules.rationale: This is the field that makes a Mudarabah placement truthful: marking it capital-guaranteed would be a false statement about an amount the counterparty does not owe.

rules.statement: A Wakala placement marked capital-guaranteed needs Shariah review.
rules.citation: The research names ACCOUNT_HOLDER as loss bearer for Mudarabah and Musharakah specifically, citing SS 13 §8/7 and SS 45 §3/4; WAKALA IS NOT NAMED in that citation and AAOIFI SS 46 (Wakala) was NOT obtained by clause in this research.
rules.rationale: Deliberately a flag and not a reject, in contrast to ISB-LQM-07, precisely because the citation does not cover Wakala. The difference between these two adjacent rules is the citation, and that is the point.

rules.citation: none — a coverage breach is a supervisory matter to be recorded and escalated, never a reason to refuse the write that records it

rules.statement: Maturity buckets must be well-formed.

serviceDomains.name: Halal Equity Screening
serviceDomains.summary: One screening result per security, with the screen itself carried as DATA. The design answer to the area guidance is this: the SSB-approved thresholds are SNAPSHOTTED onto every result (so the verdict is replayable), the method authority and source reference are REQUIRED fields, and the rules refuse a result whose authority is missing. Three outcomes only — Pass, Fail, Refer — because the research is explicit that there must be a referral path and never a silent pass. Every ratio is exact integer basis points; the denominator basis is an explicit enum because published sources genuinely differ on it and it changes the answer.

fields.name: screeningPolicyRef
fields.note: the SSB-approved policy this result applied

fields.name: screeningPolicyVersion
fields.note: the research is explicit: record the list/policy version used in the decision, or the decision is not replayable

fields.name: screeningStandardCitationVerified
fields.note: FOR THIS PROJECT, TODAY, THIS IS FALSE WHEN screeningStandardCited = AAOIFI_SS_21. The research states plainly that the widely-quoted 30/30/5 thresholds 'come only from vendor and commentary sites in this research; the primary text was not obtained'. This field exists so the citation's own status travels with every verdict.

fields.name: thresholdAuthorityName
fields.note: REQUIRED. The named SSB, scholar or index provider whose thresholds these are. No authority, no verdict — see ISB-EQS-01.

fields.name: thresholdSourceRef
fields.note: REQUIRED. Resolution number, document reference or methodology URL.

fields.name: businessActivityToleranceBps
fields.note: SNAPSHOTTED threshold, exact bps (e.g. 500 = 5%). Snapshotted rather than referenced so the verdict can be re-derived after the policy changes.

fields.name: debtRatioDenominatorBasis
fields.note: LOAD-BEARING AND GENUINELY DIVERGENT. Published methodologies differ on whether the debt ratio's denominator is a trailing-12-month average market cap, spot market cap or total assets, and the choice flips borderline securities. It is therefore data with an authority, never a constant.

fields.name: minimumCoverageForPassBps
fields.note: the data-coverage floor below which a Pass is not permitted and the result must be Refer — see ISB-EQS-04

fields.name: roundingPolicy
fields.note: a ratio sitting exactly on a threshold is decided by the rounding policy, so the policy is recorded with the result rather than left to the implementation

fields.name: screeningOutcome
fields.note: EXACTLY three, matching the research's ALLOW / REFER / BLOCK model. 'Refer' is not optional: the research's instruction is to 'Output a confidence/coverage signal and a REFER path, never a silent ALLOW.'

fields.name: dataCoverageBps
fields.note: the confidence/coverage signal the research requires — exact bps of the screen's inputs that were actually available

fields.name: externalVendorAsOf
fields.note: the research: treat a provider's verdict as DATA with a source and an asOf, never as an authority

fields.name: responsibilityRetainedByInstitution
fields.note: must be true — IFSB-31 Principle 8, quoted in the research: IIFS 'maintain full responsibility for compliance even where activities are outsourced'

fields.name: nextReviewDueDate
fields.note: IFSB-31 Principle 9 requires ONGOING compliance, so a screening result with no next review is not a control

rules.statement: A screening verdict must name the authority behind its thresholds and a source for them.
rules.citation: IFSB-31 Principle 9 (Screening), quoted in the research: 'Supervisors should determine that IIFS implement and maintain adequate policies, processes and controls to ensure ongoing compliance of investments with approved screening criteria' — and the research's own gloss: 'approved screening criteria' means the criteria come from the governance organ, the system enforces them.
rules.rationale: THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE IN THIS BUSINESS AREA. An unattributed halal/haram verdict is precisely the compliance claim the code cannot back. This rule is why the thresholds are snapshotted onto the result rather than merely referenced.

pass.thresholdAuthorityName: Dow Jones Islamic Market Shari'ah Supervisory Board

rules.statement: The institution retains Shariah responsibility even when screening is outsourced.
rules.citation: IFSB-31 Principle 8, quoted verbatim in the research: 'Supervisors should require that IIFS and issuers maintain full responsibility for compliance even where activities are outsourced.' The research adds: 'A TPP/aggregator or an external screening vendor does not transfer Shariah responsibility.'

rules.statement: A vendor-sourced result must name the vendor and the as-of.
rules.citation: Research: 'Treat the provider's verdict as data with a source and asOf, never as an authority.'

rules.statement: A Pass requires sufficient data coverage; otherwise the result is Refer.
rules.citation: Research: 'Output a confidence/coverage signal and a REFER path, never a silent ALLOW.' IFSB-31 Principle 9 requires controls for ongoing compliance.
rules.rationale: The coverage floor is itself policy data (minimumCoverageForPassBps), so the rule enforces the SSB's own threshold rather than a number this agent chose.

rules.statement: Unavailable financials cannot yield a Pass or a Fail.
rules.citation: Research: never a silent ALLOW; and a Fail on absent data is equally an unbacked claim.

rules.statement: The prohibited-revenue ratio must be derivable from its inputs to the basis point.
rules.assert: present(prohibitedActivityRatioBps) and present(totalRevenueMinor) and totalRevenueMinor > 0 implies (prohibitedActivityRevenueMinor * 10000 >= prohibitedActivityRatioBps * totalRevenueMinor and prohibitedActivityRevenueMinor * 10000 <= (prohibitedActivityRatioBps + 1) * totalRevenueMinor)
rules.citation: none — arithmetic integrity. DESIGN.md §5.1 and §6: no float in a money path.
rules.rationale: Written as a two-sided integer inequality rather than an equality for a specific reason: it checks the ratio to within one basis point WITHOUT any division, so there is no rounding step for a bug to hide in. This is the shape every derived-ratio check in this catalog should take.

rules.statement: Prohibited revenue above the tolerance cannot Pass.
rules.assert: present(prohibitedActivityRatioBps) and prohibitedActivityRatioBps > businessActivityToleranceBps implies screeningOutcome != 'Pass'
rules.citation: IFSB-31 Principle 9 — the system enforces the approved criteria. The TOLERANCE is the SSB's number (snapshotted on the record); what this rule enforces is only that the verdict follows it.
rules.rationale: Note carefully what this does NOT do: it does not assert that 5% is the right tolerance. It asserts that the recorded verdict is consistent with the recorded, attributed threshold.

rules.statement: A debt ratio above the threshold cannot Pass.
rules.assert: present(debtRatioBps) and debtRatioBps > debtRatioThresholdBps implies screeningOutcome != 'Pass'
rules.citation: IFSB-31 Principle 9 as above. The threshold and its denominator basis are both snapshotted policy data.

rules.statement: Interest-bearing assets above the threshold cannot Pass.
rules.assert: present(interestBearingAssetsRatioBps) and interestBearingAssetsRatioBps > interestBearingAssetsThresholdBps implies screeningOutcome != 'Pass'
rules.citation: IFSB-31 Principle 9 as above.

rules.statement: Illiquid assets below the stated minimum should prevent a Pass.
rules.assert: present(illiquidAssetsMinimumBps) and present(illiquidAssetsRatioBps) and illiquidAssetsRatioBps < illiquidAssetsMinimumBps implies screeningOutcome != 'Pass'
rules.citation: The tangible-asset / tradability condition on shares is a divergent position between methodologies. NO primary text was obtained in this research.
rules.rationale: flag, not reject, because unlike the three thresholds above, this condition is not universally part of a screen at all — so enforcing it would impose one school's screen on every user.

rules.statement: A result citing AAOIFI SS 21 must mark whether that citation was verified.
rules.citation: The research states it plainly: "AAOIFI SS 21's widely-quoted 30/30/5 screening thresholds come only from vendor and commentary sites in this research; the primary text was not obtained ... Make the formula configuration, with the chosen authority named."
rules.rationale: A rule whose entire purpose is honesty about this project's own citations. Today, in this estate, it FIRES — because screeningStandardCitationVerified is false until someone obtains the primary text. That is the correct behaviour: the flag is the project telling the truth about itself, and it will keep firing until the citation is real.

rules.statement: A Fail must state at least one reason.
rules.citation: Research, on the gate: record 'the decision (ALLOW/REFER/BLOCK) with the rule ID that fired'. A verdict with no reason is not an audit record.

rules.statement: A Refer must be routed to the Shariah function.
rules.citation: Research: REFER means 'queue to the Shariah compliance function'. IFSB-31 Principles 9 and 10 (research-supported).

rules.statement: A purification ratio must name its method authority and formula.
rules.citation: Research: sources 'openly disagree on the purification formula (per-share impermissible income vs ratio applied to received dividends plus realised gains) and on whether capital gains are purified at all. Make the formula configuration, with the chosen authority named.'

rules.statement: A disagreement with the vendor's verdict must be recorded as a reason.
rules.assert: present(externalVendorVerdict) and externalVendorVerdict != screeningOutcome and externalVendorVerdict != 'NotCovered' implies exists(reasonCodes, code == 'VendorDisagreement')
rules.citation: Research: a provider's verdict is data, never an authority — so a divergence is a fact to record, not an error to suppress.

rules.statement: A superseded result must point at its successor.
rules.citation: IFSB-31 Principle 11 — change of compliance status for issuers of Shariah-compliant securities (research-supported).

rules.statement: A screening result must schedule its next review.
rules.citation: IFSB-31 Principle 9 — ONGOING compliance of investments with approved screening criteria (quoted in the research). A one-shot screen is not a control.

rules.statement: A prohibited-activity breakdown must reconcile to the total.
rules.citation: none — ledger identity

rules.statement: Mixing market-cap and reporting currencies needs an explicit conversion decision.
rules.citation: DESIGN.md §6 — a ratio whose numerator and denominator are in different currencies passes through the ONE conversion function with its ISO 4217 exponent table; it must never be computed inline.
rules.rationale: Non-trivial in practice: a debt ratio with debt in the reporting currency over a market cap in the listing currency is a silent FX error dressed as a compliance threshold.

rules.statement: Every review-history entry must record the policy version it applied.
rules.citation: Research: 'Record the list version used in the decision.' Without it, a status change cannot be explained as policy-driven or fact-driven.

standards.status: EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIED. The research states the thresholds 'come only from vendor and commentary sites in this research; the primary text was not obtained'. This fragment therefore hardcodes NO threshold anywhere: every threshold is a required data field with a required named authority, and ISB-EQS-11 flags any result that cites SS 21 without a verified citation.

uncertain: NO SCREENING THRESHOLD IS HARDCODED ANYWHERE IN THIS ENTRY, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN, NOT AN OMISSION. The frequently quoted 30/30/5 numbers appear in this fragment only inside rule EXAMPLES, as illustrative test data. Baking them into the schema would be asserting an authority the research explicitly says was not obtained.

The debt-ratio denominator basis (trailing-12-month average market cap vs spot market cap vs total assets) genuinely differs between published methodologies and flips borderline securities. It is modelled as a required enum with an authority; this agent does not know which is correct and does not pretend to.

The prohibited-activity category enum is a modelled set. Whether hotels, music/cinema, defence or conventional insurance belong on it differs between methodologies, and several methodologies subdivide further. Treat the enum as configuration surface and expect an SSB to amend it.

The purification formula is absent by design. Published sources conflict on per-share impermissible income vs a ratio over received dividends plus realised gains, and on whether capital gains are purified at all. The entry carries purificationRatioBps plus a REQUIRED method authority and formula reference, and computes nothing.

SECTOR CODE IS A COARSE PROXY AND THE SAME FAILURE MODE AS MCC APPLIES. The research warns about MCC: 'a mixed merchant carries one code ... Never present an MCC pass as a halal determination.' A single GICS or ICB code on a diversified issuer has the identical weakness. This is exactly why dataCoverageBps, the Refer outcome and ISB-EQS-04 exist, and why a sector code alone can never produce a Pass here.

Screening of SUKUK as opposed to equities reuses this domain only via complianceSourceRef on a holding. A sukuk screen asks different questions (the underlying asset, the obligor, the structure) and arguably needs its own control record. Reported as a gap rather than stretched to fit.
No look-through for funds, holding companies or index constituents. A fund's or conglomerate's own holdings are not screened, so a Pass on the parent says nothing about the subsidiaries.

Effective-dating is modelled as thresholdsEffectiveFrom/To on the snapshot plus an append-only reviewHistory. A true bi-temporal model (what did we believe, as at when) is stronger and is not implemented.

areaLevelFindings.domainListSource: read out of catalog/islamic-service-landscape.json businessAreas['Treasury Markets and Sukuk'] and cross-checked against ISLAMIC-MASTER-CATALOG.md lines 572-700. No domain was invented and none was dropped.
whatCouldNotBeModelledMechanically: AGGREGATE / GROUP-BY PREDICATES. 'No single issuer above N bps of the portfolio' is not expressible as a predicate over one control record, and inventing a groupSum operator for a handful of cases would put a query engine inside a rules DSL. Concentration is therefore computed by a read projection and RECORDED in a limitBreaches sub-resource whose integrity the rules guard. If write-time aggregate enforcement is wanted, the catalog schema needs a first-class `aggregates` block and the template a query generator — that is a §8 schema decision for the design owner, not something to smuggle in as a free-text assert.
CROSS-ARRAY MEMBERSHIP. Comparing a position's structure against membership of a sibling permittedStructures array is a join, not a per-record predicate. Same resolution as above.

CROSS-SERVICE INVARIANTS. A holding's debtBasedUnderlying must match its issuance program's structure, and a portfolio position's compliance status must match the screening result it cites. Each service owns its own database, so no rule can read across. These are modelled as denormalised fields kept current by the events in this fragment, and the staleness window is real and unaddressed.

ROUNDING TOLERANCE IN A CROSS-CURRENCY CHECK. ISB-WAD-04 can be written exactly using minorUnitScale() on both currencies, but whether exact equality holds depends on a rounding policy that lives in the single money-conversion module of DESIGN.md §6. It is a `flag` until that policy and its property-based tests exist, and should be promoted to `reject` afterwards.

PER / IRR. Smoothing reserves are cited (IFSB-30 ¶256, GN-3 ¶20/25-27) and deliberately NOT modelled in this area even though a Mudarabah-managed sukuk portfolio is where they bite, because the appropriation ORDER is normative and must be owned in exactly one place — the Deposits area's isb-profit-equalization-reserve and isb-investment-risk-reserve. Cross-area coordination needed. BNM ¶13.5 forbids smoothing outright, so it must also be feature-flaggable per jurisdiction.
gapsInDESIGNmd7ToRaise: The ContractType enum has ten values and three of the seven domains here cannot use any of them. Tawarruq (isb-interbank-commodity-murabaha-desk) is absent from §7 although the research's own recommended enum includes TAWARRUQ. A currency exchange (Sarf) and a promise (Wa'd) are both absent, which is why isb-islamic-fx-wad-arrangements carries contractType: null. RECOMMENDATION: §7's enum should gain Tawarruq and Sarf, and `promiseType` should be a dimension beside contractType rather than a value inside it. This fragment does NOT invent those values — it reports the gap and sets null, because a wrong value in a compliance field is worse than an absent one.

§8's catalog example shows `rules: [{id, assert, onViolation}]` with assert as a string. That is honoured literally here, but the string has to be in a closed grammar for a rules component to be generatable from it, so this fragment defines one (conventions.ruleAssertGrammar) and every assert parses. If the design owner prefers a structured AST, that is a one-time §8 amendment — but prose asserts cannot be generated and should not be accepted from any area fragment.

§8's `onViolation: reject|flag` has no third value, while the research's screening model has three outcomes (ALLOW/REFER/BLOCK). This fragment maps REFER onto `flag` (accept + finding + audit row + referral) rather than inventing a value. Worth confirming that reading.
generatorWorkThisFragmentImplies: A ~60-line recursive-descent parser + evaluator for conventions.ruleAssertGrammar, with int64 overflow-checked arithmetic and NO division operator.
A minorUnitScale() builtin backed by the ONE ISO 4217 exponent table of DESIGN.md §6 — the same table the Go/Java money boundary uses, not a second copy.
`ratio` and `rate` emitted as two int64 columns each with CHECK constraints, including the denominator cap that keeps cross-multiplication inside int64.
`array` fields emitted as child tables with a parent FK and ON DELETE CASCADE, and as nested OpenAPI schemas; behaviourQualifiers emitted as the sub-resource paths over them.
Append-only enforcement for the sub-resources marked so (no PUT/DELETE on shariahFindings or reviewHistory) — DESIGN.md §5.8.
Two generated tests per rule from examples.pass / examples.fail.
